newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was generally weak on moderate to fairly good demand and moderate to heavy offerings, USDA said.

Demand for retail and HRI needs was fairly good for post holiday featuring needs. Higher price levels was fairly consistent on the loin cuts most of the week, but did show some weakness late in the trading period.

Rib cuts were generally under pressure all week, with the most weakness on the Choice rib cuts. Chuck and rounds were under downward pressure all week, while the most losses were again on the Choice cuts.

Closely trimmed items followed somewhat the same pattern as the commodity product, chuck and round cuts traded lower and the loin cuts were firm. Beef trimmings were generally higher on improved demand as the week progressed.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on the percentages grinds, but the chuck and round grinds were lower on light to moderate demand.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal steady to 2.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal 1.50 to 4.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal 2.00 to 3.00 lower; Select and Choice loin primal 3.00 to 4.00 higher; Closely trimmed items 1.00 lower; Beef trimmings 1.50 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items steady to 2.00 lower.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.49 at 103.70; 700/850 Dn 1.13 at 103.02; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.14 at 97.84; 700/850 Dn 1.15 at 97.45.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT As spring field work approaches in the Northern and Southeastern regions, slaughter cow numbers increased. With retail grinding demand being moderate to good the lean boneless beef prices rebounded after trading significantly lower last week.

The South Central area is still experiencing light slaughter cow receipts thus causing lean boneless beef to trade sharply higher in the Texas area. In addition, Utility cow carcasses traded higher on light to moderate demand and offerings. Furthermore, the 100% lean market finished the week sharply higher after moving firm early. The increase in the 100% lean market was driven by very light supplies and moderate to good demand as buyers struggled to cover needs.

Breaking Utility carcasses 3.00-4.00 higher; Boning Utility 2.00-3.00; Cutter not established; 90% boneless beef 6.00 higher in the Midwest, Texas 10.00 higher; 85% 6.00-9.00 higher; 75% 2.00 lower; 65% 2.00 higher.
The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, March 27, 1997 was estimated at 84.67 per cwt., up 3.92 from a week ago Friday.
